newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian oil export staff threaten strike.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian oil export staff threaten strike.

text.p: Workers of Nigeria's Department of Petroleum Resources (DPR) which processes export documents for oil shipments have threatened to go on strike from Friday if the backlog of their salaries are not paid, oil ministry sources said on Tuesday.

"They have told the minister of petroleum resources that they will strike if their January pay is not forthcoming by Friday," said a ministry official. "The minister is working to resolve the situation," he added.

DPR staff have been unhappy since last summer when the Nigerian military government contracted outside inspectors to check oil shipments following allegations of overloading tankers to rob the government of oil revenues.
The official said salaries from January for DPR workers were pending and it was expected that they would be paid along with those of this month.
"Whether or not they will actually go on strike I do not know but they have told the authorities that they will if their salaries are not paid by the end of this month," he said.
The oil unions have been powerless since 1994 when the military government sacked and detained their leaders over a two-month strike in support of presidential claimant Moshood Abiola.
"The strike threat involves DPR staff and not unions," the official said.
He said it was not clear whether oil exports would be disrupted if the strike materialised. "It is possible there are other staff that can take over documentation but we have to wait and see."
